records.completion_scope: The chosen Pike Brook opening, Branch River and pond passages, Salmon Falls corridor, lower Piscataqua estuary and both distinct New Castle/Portsmouth Harbor endings are covered at ordinary geographic scale. Piscataqua River is supported only as the representative receiving-system name.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative lower receiving-system identity for the fully researched connected Pike Brook–Branch River–pond chain–Salmon Falls–Piscataqua/Portsmouth Harbor composite. scope_limits: The representative identity does not rename Pike Brook, Branch River, Salmon Falls River, Union Meadows or any named pond. No formal names registry was consulted.

Selected positions are generalized orientation, not surveyed banks or a requirement that every straight segment is presently wetted. Branch-mouth, pond-shore and terminal island shortcuts are retained as generalization rather than repaired.

The source ending and rendered ending differ within the western New Castle/Portsmouth Harbor receiving setting. The final segment is not represented as the main navigation channel, a natural-river mouth coordinate or an open-Atlantic endpoint.
The maps establish ordinary connected river, pond and tidal-harbor geography, not current flow, tidal height, impoundment operation or legal name boundaries.
Four views are one primary cartographic publication, with composite epochs and scale-dependent naming. Reading aids supply no independent geographic evidence.

records.region: Vancouver Island, Great Central Lake and Somass receiving system
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-system identity only; Great Central Lake and the separately named Stamp River are not aliases of Somass River.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected northwestern mountain feeder, Great Central Lake passage, Stamp receiving corridor and lower Somass reach form a researched composite represented by its named receiving system. The selected initial feeder remains separately unnamed in this finding.
records.completion_scope: Both selected mainstem fragments and all 45 stored parts have ordinary terrain-scale correspondence: northwestern mountain hollow and southeast feeder, entry into Great Central Lake, full lake passage, eastern outlet and northward Stamp corridor, downstream receiving river, and actual Alberni Inlet ending. NHC authorial prose independently identifies Great Central Lake draining by Stamp River, the Stamp–Sproat junction forming Somass River, and Somass entering Alberni Inlet. Somass River is supported as a representative receiving-system name, with the lake and upper river kept as bounded components.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected northwestern mountain feeder, Great Central Lake passage, Stamp receiving corridor and lower Somass reach form a researched composite represented by its named receiving system. The selected initial feeder remains separately unnamed in this finding.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
